content: If you miss a dose of this medication, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is close to the time of your next scheduled dose, skip the missed dose and proceed with your regular dosing schedule. Do not double the dose to make up for the missed one. Store this medication at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Avoid storing it in the bathroom. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless specifically instructed to do so. Properly dispose of this product when it is expired or no longer needed. Sodium bicarbonate is used to reduce stomach acid. It acts as a fast-acting antacid to relieve symptoms of heartburn, indigestion, and upset stomach. However, it should only be used for temporary relief. Take this medication orally, usually every four hours as needed or as directed by your doctor. Some tablets must be dissolved in a glass of water before swallowing, while others can be swallowed whole or dissolved in water. Follow the instructions on the product packaging carefully. If you are self-treating and your symptoms persist or worsen after two weeks of use, or if you suspect a serious medical problem, seek medical attention immediately. If you are using this medication daily for more than two weeks, consult your doctor, as you may have an underlying medical condition requiring different treatment. If your doctor has prescribed this medication for acidosis or to alkalinize your urine, the dosage will depend on your medical condition and response to treatment. To maximize the benefits, take the medication regularly and exactly as directed. It is typically taken several times a day. To help you remember, take it at the same times each day. Common side effects may include nausea, bloating, or gas. If your doctor has prescribed this medication, they have determined that the benefits outweigh the risks of side effects. When taken with sodium bicarbonate, large amounts of calcium from your diet, medications, or supplements can rarely cause a serious condition called milk-alkali syndrome. Consult your doctor or pharmacist about using calcium products safely while on this medication. Severe allergic reactions to this drug are rare. This is not a complete list of possible side effects. In the U.S., contact your doctor for medical advice about side effects. In Canada, consult your doctor for medical advice about side effects. Before taking sodium bicarbonate, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it or if you have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could cause allergic reactions or other problems. During pregnancy, this medication should only be used when clearly needed, as it may worsen high blood pressure during pregnancy. This medication may also pass into breast milk. Drug interactions can alter how your medications work or increase the risk of serious side effects. Keep a list of all the products you use, including prescription and non-prescription drugs and herbal products, and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. Sodium bicarbonate can reduce the effectiveness of certain drugs that require stomach acid to work, such as ampicillin, atazanavir, certain azole antifungals (e.g., ketoconazole, itraconazole), iron supplements, pazopanib, and sucralfate, among others. If your doctor has advised you to take low-dose aspirin to prevent heart attack or stroke (usually 81-162 milligrams per day), continue taking it unless instructed otherwise. In case of an overdose, if someone has severe symptoms such as passing out or difficulty breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222, and Canadian residents can call 1-844-764-7669. If you are taking large doses of this medication or using it for more than two weeks, laboratory and/or medical tests (e.g., calcium, potassium, sodium, bicarbonate levels) should be performed to monitor your condition. Keep all medical and laboratory appointments.
